findings: BLOCKING (privacy): configs/pilot/agents-unattended.toml grants the unattended codex author sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true and the claude reviewer WebSearch/WebFetch under --permission-mode dontAsk, while execute() inlines the full bound context (campaign docs, SPEC, run.py, aggregate bundle contents) into their prompts. The 'no remote writes' constraint is instruction-only, so either agent can exfiltrate the bound context. Disable network for these stages or stop inlining file contents.

BLOCKING (authority/identity binding): in campaign_pipeline.execute(), author and reviewer share the same round-N directory and the author runs first with workspace write. Nothing in the supplied source prevents the codex author from pre-writing review.json with verdict APPROVE, which would satisfy the opposing-family gate without the claude reviewer authoring it. Assert review.json is absent before the reviewer stage or run the reviewer in a separate directory; verify run_isolated_stage's fresh-output semantics.

BLOCKING (fail-open guard): colab-worker-future.json invokes the hook via bare 'python' at a hardcoded absolute path; if 'python' is not on PATH the command exits 127, a non-blocking PreToolUse error, so get_cells proceeds with outputs and the privacy guard is silently disabled. Additionally the allow list is the wildcard mcp__colab-worker__* while the guard covers only get_cells, so any other tool returning cell outputs bypasses PILOT_OUTPUT_READ_BLOCKED. Use python3 and allow-list only guarded tools. (The guard function itself is correctly fail-closed on includeOutputs and malformed input.)

Recovery semantics: grounding() and the request.json write occur before the evidence-preserving try in execute(); a grounding failure leaves the output directory with no blocked.json, and mkdir(exist_ok=False) then rejects reruns at that path with no recorded reason.

Receipt binding gaps: artifact_sha256 uses non-recursive directory.iterdir(), leaving subdirectory artifacts unbound; P002/P003 receipts do not record the predecessor interpretation_receipt.json hash they were gated on, so the verified predecessor state is not provable from the receipt.

Minor hygiene: system_stage leaks one mkdtemp config directory per stage and mutates module-global sc.ROOT (not concurrency-safe); grounding reads predecessor files without the symlink check applied to other inputs.

Positive: scientific-approval preservation is correct — only *.proposed.* artifacts are written under pipeline/, experiments/ is never modified (test asserts run.py untouched), and all persisted statuses honestly disclaim human ratification. efficiency_review.py copies only whitelisted fields and records worker receipts by digest.

Caveat: source-only review; run_isolated_stage and orchestrator.publication.inventory were not supplied, so fresh-output enforcement, receipt 'ci' semantics, and bundle-name handling in inventory() could not be verified. No tests were executed.
